From 2397e9264676be7794f8f7f1e9763d90bd3c7335 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Taeyang Lee <0wn@theori.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 16:03:58 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: authencesn - reject too-short AAD (assoclen<8) to
 match ESP/ESN spec

authencesn assumes an ESP/ESN-formatted AAD. When assoclen is shorter than
the minimum expected length, crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt() can advance past
the end of the destination scatterlist and trigger a NULL pointer dereference
in scatterwalk_map_and_copy(), leading to a kernel panic (DoS).

Add a minimum AAD length check to fail fast on invalid inputs.

Fixes: 104880a6b470 ("crypto: authencesn - Convert to new AEAD interface")
Reported-By: Taeyang Lee <0wn@theori.io>
Signed-off-by: Taeyang Lee <0wn@theori.io>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/crypto/authencesn.c b/crypto/authencesn.c
index d1bf0fda3f2e..542a978663b9 100644
--- a/crypto/authencesn.c
+++ b/crypto/authencesn.c
@@ -169,6 +169,9 @@ static int crypto_authenc_esn_encrypt(struct aead_request *req)
 	struct scatterlist *src, *dst;
 	int err;
 
+	if (assoclen < 8)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	sg_init_table(areq_ctx->src, 2);
 	src = scatterwalk_ffwd(areq_ctx->src, req->src, assoclen);
 	dst = src;
@@ -256,6 +259,9 @@ static int crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt(struct aead_request *req)
 	u32 tmp[2];
 	int err;
 
+	if (assoclen < 8)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	cryptlen -= authsize;
 
 	if (req->src != dst)
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies **crypto/authencesn.c** to add a minimal AAD length check. Specifically:

- In `crypto_authenc_esn_encrypt()`, a check `if (assoclen < 8) return -EINVAL;` is added before the main logic.
- In `crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt()`, the same check `if (assoclen < 8) return -EINVAL;` is added before processing the decrypt request.

Both checks ensure that the associated data (AAD) length is at least 8 bytes, as required by the ESP/ESN specification. This prevents a potential NULL pointer dereference in `scatterwalk_map_and_copy()` that could occur when `assoclen` is too short, by failing early with an `-EINVAL` error. The changes are functionally identical in both the encrypt and decrypt paths, enforcing the same constraint to maintain correctness and security.

This function does not include the required check `if (assoclen < 8) return -EINVAL;` before those operations. Therefore, when `assoclen` is less than 8, it can lead to a NULL pointer dereference and kernel panic, exactly as described in the root cause.
